originals.ko: 나는 한 달 동안 배워 왔어
originals.why: Natural North Welsh. It uses the perfect-progressive in the sense this LEGO teaches.

originals.ko: 나는 한 달 동안 이야기하는 것을 배워 왔어
originals.why: dysgu siarad means 'learning to speak'. Natural and idiomatic.

originals.ko: 나는 웨일스어로 이야기하는 것을 배워 왔어
originals.why: Natural. Same sense as the LEGO.

originals.ko: 나는 한 달 동안 내가 할 수 있는 만큼 열심히 배워 왔어
originals.why: Natural word order, with the adverbial before am fis.

originals.ko: 나는 내가 얼마나 빨리 배워 왔는지 알아냈으면 좋겠어
originals.why: Natural embedded clause after pa mor gyflym. The Korean says liciwn i as ~했으면 좋겠어 so it does not clash with dw i isio (~하고 싶어).

originals.ko: 나는 내가 얼마나 빨리 배워 왔는지 확실하지 않아

topups.ko: 나는 웨일스어를 아주 잘 하지 않지만 내가 할 수 있는 만큼 열심히 배워 왔어
나는 지금 웨일스어를 조금 할 수 있어 왜냐하면 나는 배워 왔으니까

topups.why: Valid, but only 2 USE top-ups are needed and U04 and U05 use the LEGO in fuller contexts.
'오늘 오후에 ~배워 왔어' sounds awkward in Korean as a perfect-progressive.
Valid, but not needed. Fewer is fine.
The meaning is muddled: a question about tonight whose reason is the speaker's own learning reads oddly.

originals.why: Natural North Welsh with the contracted ’di. It matches the seed.
Natural. am tua wythnos is used in the duration sense this LEGO teaches.
Natural ti ’di bod yn. Correct sense.

originals.ko: 나는 일주일 정도 이야기하는 연습을 할 거야

topups.ko: 너는 일주일 정도 웨일스어를 배워 왔어?

topups.why: Valid, but only 1 BUILD is needed.
'나와 일주일 정도' is a fragment that sounds awkward in Korean.
Valid, but not needed. Its Korean also lacks the explicit 나는.

refill.why: Grammatical, but only 1 BUILD is needed and B04 is the stronger phrase.
'나와 일주일 정도' is an awkward fragment in Korean. It could mean 'with me' or 'and me', so the learner can't tell which Welsh to say.
